topic.name: Quadratic Equations with Purely Imaginary Solutions

question.explanation:
First, we rearrange the equation, as follows: \[ \eqalign{ 6q^2 + 2 &= 0 \\[5pt] 6q^2 &= -2\\[5pt] q^2 & = -\dfrac{2}{6}\\[5pt] q^2 & = -\dfrac{1}{3} } \]

By taking square root, we obtain: \[ q = \pm \sqrt{-\dfrac{1}{3}} \]

We now rewrite $q$ using the imaginary unit $\textrm{i}=\sqrt{-1}\, \mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} q & = \pm \sqrt{-\dfrac{1}{3}}\\[5pt] & = \pm \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{3} \cdot (-1)}\\[5pt] & = \pm \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{3}} \cdot \sqrt{-1}\\[5pt] & = \pm \dfrac{\sqrt{1}}{\sqrt{3}} \cdot \sqrt{-1}\\[5pt] & = \pm \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \textrm{i} \end{align}

Finally, we rationalize the denominator:

\begin{align} q &= \pm \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \textrm{i}\\[5pt] & = \pm \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}} \cdot \sqrt{-1}\\[5pt] & = \pm \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \textrm{i} \end{align}

question.explanation:
First, we rearrange the equation, as follows: \[ \eqalign{ 16y^2 + 4 & = 0\\[5pt] 16y^2 & = -4 \\[5pt] y^2 & = -\dfrac{4}{16}\\[5pt] y^2 & = -\dfrac{1}{4} } \]

By taking square root, we obtain:

\[ y = \pm \sqrt{-\dfrac{1}{4}} \]

We now rewrite $y$ using the imaginary unit $\textrm{i}=\sqrt{-1}\, \mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} y & = \pm \sqrt{-\dfrac{1}{4}}\\[5pt] & = \pm \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{4} \cdot (-1)}\\[5pt] & = \pm \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{4}} \cdot \sqrt{-1}\\[5pt] & = \pm \dfrac{\sqrt{1}}{\sqrt{4}} \cdot \sqrt{-1}\\[5pt] & = \pm \dfrac{1}{2} \textrm{i} \end{align}

question.explanation:
First, we rearrange the equation, as follows: \[ \eqalign{ 25p^2 + 9 & = 0\\[5pt] 25p^2 & = -9 \\[5pt] p^2 & = -\dfrac{9}{25} } \]

By taking square root, we obtain:

\[ p = \pm \sqrt{-\dfrac{9}{25}} \]

We now rewrite $p$ using the imaginary unit $\textrm{i}=\sqrt{-1}\, \mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} p & = \pm \sqrt{-\dfrac{9}{25}}\\[5pt] & = \pm \sqrt{\dfrac{9}{25} \cdot (-1)}\\[5pt] & = \pm \sqrt{\dfrac{9}{25}} \cdot \sqrt{-1}\\[5pt] & = \pm \dfrac{\sqrt{9}}{\sqrt{25}} \cdot \sqrt{-1}\\[5pt] & = \pm \dfrac{3}{5} \textrm{i} \end{align}
